newsitem.title: USA: NY physical coffee - summer doldrums persist.
newsitem.headline: NY physical coffee - summer doldrums persist.

text.p: The New York physical coffee spreads showed some signs of easing this week, but only scattered spot sales were noted as processors kept to the sidelines, traders said.

Traders noted roastings have slowed as North America neared mid-summer, when coffee consumption typically drops off. Additionally, many roasting plants routinely shut down in July for preventive maintenance.
"It's been very quiet," said one dealer. "Roasters are pretty well covered into September and fill-ins are the only thing you see."

Spot Colombian differentials softened, but failed to tempt many buyers who still viewed the beans as expensive. Traders said many roasters have been cutting back on Colombian coffees in their blends as a cost-saving measure.
"Roasters are switching out of Colombians," said one trader. "And I think that has contributed to the easing of differentials."
Spot Colombians MAMs were heard at 25 cents over "C", down some five cents in the past two weeks. Supremos, also on the spot market, garnered some 30 cents over "C".
Colombians forward delivery, however, attracted more interest, with Colombians for October-December shipment fetching 22 cents over the CSCE December contract.

Differentials on Brazilian coffees, which are in the midst of harvesting, also eased. Spot Santos 4s were a cent or two weaker this week, at 11-12 cents under "C". Santos 2/3s were offered at two-to-four cents under "C".

Traders said, however, supplies of many quality coffees were still very tight ahead of harvest in the autumn, with few quotes heard for Central American beans. Small quantities of spot prime guatemalans were heard at 13 over "C", while hard bean Guatemalans were offered at some 25 cents over "C".
CSCE July coffee rose 3.50 cents a lb Friday to settle at 186.00. September ended 2.40 cents higher at 164.10.
